title: Declare the existing Homebrew baseline in nix-darwin
description: Add a Darwin Homebrew module that declares the currently required taps, requested formulae, and all 15 casks. Do not migrate or uninstall tools in this step. Keep onActivation.autoUpdate and upgrade conservative and cleanup disabled so the first activation is additive and reversible. Remove only taps proven unused by the declared inventory.
acceptance_criteria: darwin-rebuild build succeeds; activating produces no unintended removals; all current casks and required custom formulae remain installed; and brew bundle check reports the declared baseline satisfied.
notes:
Implemented review candidate: added modules/darwin/homebrew.nix and imported it from hosts/macbook-pro/default.nix. Declares 57 requested brews, all 15 casks, and 7 taps proven required by declared custom packages. Keeps autoUpdate=false, upgrade=false, cleanup=none. Custom Homebrew 6 trust declarations use homebrew.extraConfig because nix-darwin 25.11 lacks typed trusted fields. Safe validation passed: nix flake check path:/Users/scaf/.config/nix-conf --all-systems --no-build; full Darwin system build with --no-link; generated Brewfile inventory parity (57 brews/15 casks); HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew bundle check --no-upgrade reports dependencies satisfied; git diff --check. No activation, uninstall, cleanup, commit, push, or bead close performed pending review.
Review follow-up: alphabetized all 51 typed brew entries. Verified they are unique and sorted; flake check and git diff --check still pass. No activation or closure performed.
Completion attempt: final Darwin build after ordering fix passed. System activation is blocked because non-interactive sudo reports 'a password is required'. Human must run: sudo darwin-rebuild switch --flake 'path:/Users/scaf/.config/nix-conf#macbook-pro'. Keep bead in_progress until post-activation package/service checks pass. The two-axis code review already completed with no hard standards violations or confirmed spec defects; only activation-dependent acceptance remains.
Post-activation verification passed: /run/current-system exactly matches the expected built path; Homebrew inventory remains 235 formulae and 15 casks; generated Brewfile bundle check passes; yabai and skhd are running with last exit code 0. Final two-axis review: no blocking standards findings and spec acceptance MET.
close_reason: Implemented declarative Homebrew baseline, activated successfully, verified no package removals, passed bundle check and service checks, and completed final two-axis review.

title: Capture and classify the current Homebrew inventory
description: Record the migration baseline and classify requested packages by destination. Observed inventory: 235 formulae, 53 requested leaves, 15 casks, 12 taps, no pinned formulae, and five installed-but-inactive service definitions (dolt, herdr, php, php@8.2, unbound). The Brewfile additionally records uv tool browser-use and npm globals @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, @modelcontextprotocol/server-github, 9router, better-sqlite3, oh-my-claude-sisyphus, sql.js, systray2, and yaml-language-server. A nixpkgs availability probe found direct aarch64-darwin candidates for most standard CLIs; exceptions or uncertain identities include beads, beads_viewer, composer, firefoxpwa, flux9s, herdr, hunk, rtk, plannotator-tui, floci, and the custom omp/mole formulae.
acceptance_criteria: Counts, taps, casks, requested formulae, language-global packages, service state, and initial Nix availability are documented in this issue and can be used as the baseline for later phases.
close_reason: Inventory captured from brew leaves, brew bundle dump, taps, services, and nixpkgs aarch64-darwin availability checks.

title: Migrate Homebrew to declarative Nix management
description: Gradually make the Mac software inventory reproducible through nix-darwin and Home Manager without a disruptive one-shot migration. Current baseline: 235 installed formulae (53 leaves), 15 casks, 12 taps, no pinned formulae, and no active Homebrew services. The generated Brewfile also contains one uv tool and eight global npm packages. Preserve working tools first, move portable CLI tools to Nix in tested batches, keep macOS-native applications and unsupported/custom formulae in declarative Homebrew, then enable cleanup only after parity is verified.
design: Use nix-darwin homebrew.* as the declarative bridge. Start with cleanup disabled. Migrate one category at a time; for each package verify binary identity, version expectations, config/data paths, shell integration, and a representative command before uninstalling the Homebrew copy. Prefer Home Manager for user CLI tools, nix-darwin for machine services/system tools, and project devShells for project-specific runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: All intentionally installed brews, casks, taps, npm globals, and uv tools have an explicit owner: Nix/Home Manager, declarative Homebrew, project environment, or documented exception. A rebuild succeeds, daily tools are smoke-tested, stale dependencies/taps are removed, and bootstrap documentation matches the final configuration.
notes: Migration completed across all nine child nodes. Final state: portable CLIs are Home Manager-managed and smoke-tested; native/fast-moving/runtime exceptions are declarative Homebrew or explicitly documented mutable user tools; all 15 casks and six required taps are represented; stale formulae/dependencies/taps were removed without zap; Brewfile and dependency checks pass; active Darwin generation matches the build; clean tracked-only bootstrap validation and documentation pass; secrets remain excluded.
close_reason: All package owners are explicit, builds and daily-tool workflows pass, Homebrew converges without stale entries, and reproducible bootstrap documentation is validated.

title: Evaluate custom-tap and fast-moving tools
description:
## Goal
Check package identity, release freshness, and Darwin behavior for beads, beads_viewer, opencode, omp, flux9s, floci, herdr, hunk, mole, rtk, and plannotator-tui. Select declarative Homebrew or a maintained Nix package for each.

## Method
Compare the installed formula upstream and version with nixpkgs. Treat same-name packages as unverified until their upstream identity matches. Prefer existing trusted taps initially; only add an overlay when its maintenance burden is justified.

## Findings
Initial probing found direct nixpkgs candidates for opencode and a package named mole, but identity/version parity remains unverified. Direct aarch64-darwin candidates were not found for beads, beads_viewer, flux9s, herdr, hunk, rtk, plannotator-tui, floci, or the custom omp formula. Record final findings here during the spike.
acceptance_criteria: Every custom tool has a verified upstream identity and selected source. Unused taps are identified. Any proposed Nix package includes an update-maintenance plan; otherwise the tool remains explicitly declared in Homebrew.
notes:
## Findings

All evaluated tools remain declarative Homebrew packages. No overlay is proposed, so there is no custom Nix update-maintenance burden.

- beads — gastownhall/beads; Homebrew core; installed/stable 1.3.0; absent from pinned nixpkgs.
- beads_viewer — Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer; Homebrew core; 0.25.0; absent from pinned nixpkgs.
- opencode — anomalyco/opencode; trusted anomalyco/tap; Homebrew stable 1.18.31. nixpkgs is the same upstream but only 1.1.14, so retain Homebrew for release freshness.
- omp — omp.sh coding agent (not oh-my-posh); trusted can1357/tap; stable 18.2.1; no matching pinned nixpkgs package.
- flux9s — dgunzy/flux9s; trusted dgunzy/tap; stable 1.0.4; absent from pinned nixpkgs.
- floci — floci.io/floci; trusted floci-io/floci tap; stable 0.2.3; absent from pinned nixpkgs.
- herdr — herdr.dev; Homebrew core; stable 0.9.1; absent from pinned nixpkgs.
- hunk — hunk.dev; Homebrew core; stable 0.22.0; absent from pinned nixpkgs.
- mole — mole.fit Mac cleaner; Homebrew core; stable 1.54.0. nixpkgs `mole` is davrodpin/mole, an unrelated SSH tunnel CLI, so it must not be substituted.
- rtk — rtk-ai.app; Homebrew core; stable 0.49.0; absent from pinned nixpkgs.
- plannotator-tui — plannotator/plannotator-tui; trusted plannotator/tap; installed/stable 0.8.0; absent from pinned nixpkgs.

Every tap declared in modules/darwin/homebrew.nix has a current consumer. Previously installed but undeclared taps proven unused by the declarative inventory are derailed/k9s, hashicorp/tap, kitlangton/tap, localstack/tap, and wezterm/wezterm (wezterm@nightly now resolves from homebrew/cask). They may be removed during the cleanup bead, not during this spike.

Several installed custom tools trail their current Homebrew formula version because activation upgrades are disabled. That is intentional; upgrades must be a separate deliberate action.
close_reason: Verified upstream identity, release freshness, Darwin source, and ownership for every custom tool; retained all in declarative Homebrew and identified five unused taps for cleanup.

title: Migrate cloud, infrastructure, and developer CLIs
description: Evaluate and migrate standard development tools with direct nixpkgs candidates: ansible, awscli2, azure-cli, biome, fluxcd, gemini-cli, graphviz, imagemagick, k6, and related Kubernetes tooling. Check plugins, credential discovery, completions, and version requirements before changing ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Chosen tools are Nix-managed, authentication/config paths still work, completions are available where expected, representative workflows pass, and removed Homebrew entries have no dependent requested formulae that still require them.
notes:
Implemented pre-activation candidate: migrated ansible, awscli2, azure-cli, biome, fluxcd, graphviz, imagemagick, and k6 to Home Manager; removed corresponding Homebrew requests and fluxcd tap. Retained gemini-cli in Homebrew because nixpkgs 25.11 (0.25.2) materially trails installed Homebrew (0.46.0), documented in code. Flake check, full no-link build, generated Brewfile and bundle check pass. Two-axis review found no blockers; activation/runtime/auth/completion checks remain.
Post-activation verification passed: active system matches expected; all 8 migrated commands resolve via Home Manager and pass smoke tests; ~/.aws ~/.azure ~/.kube remain; aws completer is present; interactive zsh exits cleanly; generated Brewfile/bundle check pass. Final two-axis review found no blockers and acceptance MET.
close_reason: Migrated eight development/cloud CLIs to Home Manager, retained lagging Gemini CLI on Homebrew, activated and verified runtime/config/completion behavior, and completed final review.

title: Choose a policy for language runtimes and global packages
description:
## Decision
Choose ownership for node, pnpm, yarn, global npm packages, Python 3.11/3.12, pyenv, pipx, PHP 8.2, composer, dotnet-sdk@8, browser-use installed through uv, and gcloud-cli.

## Rationale
Language runtimes and mutable global package ecosystems have different reproducibility and update needs from ordinary CLI tools. Blindly replacing them can break projects or remove globally installed agent tooling.

## Alternatives Considered
Home Manager packages; per-project devShells; language version managers; declarative Homebrew; or a documented hybrid. Compare version pinning, project compatibility, global tool packaging, upgrade cadence, and work-laptop portability before implementation.
design:
## Policy
Use a documented hybrid rather than forcing mutable language ecosystems into the Nix system profile.

### Node.js
- Owner: declarative Homebrew for node, pnpm, and yarn.
- Required behavior: current Homebrew Node remains the global runtime for agent tooling. Exact versions are intentionally not pinned by nix-darwin; project-specific Node versions belong in per-project devShells.
- Global npm tools retained as a documented mutable exception: @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, @modelcontextprotocol/server-github, 9router, better-sqlite3, oh-my-claude-sisyphus, sql.js, systray2, yaml-language-server, and npm itself.
- Migration order: project devShell first, then package a global tool only when reproducibility outweighs its rapid update cadence.

### Python
- Owner: declarative Homebrew for python@3.11, python@3.12, pyenv, and pipx. The unversioned python3 may be supplied transitively and is not a project contract.
- Project strategy: pin Python and dependencies in devShells; use pyenv only for non-Nix projects that require it.
- uv/browser-use: retain the existing user-local uv installation and mutable browser-use uv tool as a documented exception because browser-use is unavailable in the pinned nixpkgs Darwin set.

### PHP
- Owner: declarative Homebrew for php@8.2 and composer.
- Required version: projects needing PHP 8.2 must use the versioned Homebrew path or a project devShell; the globally linked php may be newer because Composer pulls the current PHP formula.
- Composer stays with Homebrew because its runtime coupling is already working and the global package set is mutable.

### .NET and Google Cloud
- Owner: declarative Homebrew casks dotnet-sdk@8 and gcloud-cli.
- Required version: .NET 8 must remain installed even if another SDK is selected by default. Projects pin SDK selection with global.json. gcloud remains latest-through-Homebrew to avoid stale cloud APIs/components.

## Upgrade and rollback
- Upgrade runtime/tool ecosystems deliberately with Homebrew/npm/uv, independently of darwin-rebuild.
- Roll back Nix-owned configuration by switching nix-darwin generations.
- Roll back a runtime by restoring its Homebrew declaration/versioned formula and reinstalling global npm or uv tools from the bootstrap inventory.
- Do not enable Homebrew cleanup until these retained entries and exceptions are represented in bootstrap documentation.
acceptance_criteria: A documented per-runtime decision identifies the owner, required versions, global tools to package or retain, project-local strategy, migration order, and rollback method. Follow-up implementation beads exist for decisions too large for one change.
notes: Inventory confirmed before decision: Homebrew Node/npm/pnpm/yarn, Python 3.11/3.12/pyenv/pipx, PHP/composer, dotnet-sdk@8 and gcloud casks are working; global npm inventory has eight user tools plus npm; browser-use is installed through user-local uv. Pinned nixpkgs has uv, composer, dotnet 8, and google-cloud-sdk candidates, but browser-use is unavailable and several cloud/runtime versions lag. Decision is to retain these as explicit Homebrew or mutable user-tool exceptions, with project versions owned by devShells. No implementation follow-up bead is needed because no ownership change is selected; bootstrap documentation bead 8a8.9 will record the reinstall commands.
close_reason: Documented per-runtime ownership, version strategy, global-tool exceptions, project devShell policy, migration order, and rollback method; no package ownership changes selected.

title: Migrate low-risk portable CLI tools to Home Manager
description: Move a first small batch of portable user tools from Homebrew to Home Manager, then remove those entries from homebrew.brews. Initial candidates: actionlint, age, eza, fd, fzf, gh, lazygit, ripgrep, sops, kubectx, kubernetes-helm, and mkcert. Handle shell integrations through Home Manager rather than Homebrew-sourced scripts. Keep batches small enough to identify regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Each selected command resolves to /nix/store or the Home Manager profile, representative commands work, shell startup is clean, darwin-rebuild succeeds, and the corresponding Homebrew formulae are no longer requested.
notes:
Implemented review candidate: added modules/home/cli-tools.nix with actionlint, age, eza, fd, gh, kubectx, kubernetes-helm, lazygit, mkcert, ripgrep, and sops; imported it plus existing fzf.nix in the Mac Home Manager profile; removed all 12 corresponding Homebrew requests. Safe validation passed: flake check, full no-link Darwin build, generated Brewfile excludes all 12, bundle check satisfied, git diff clean. Two-axis pre-activation review found no blockers or spec defects; added a comment documenting helm -> kubernetes-helm mapping. Activation-dependent command resolution, smoke tests, and shell startup remain. sudo requires interactive password.
First activation succeeded, but post-activation acceptance check found fresh login shells still resolved selected commands from /opt/homebrew/bin because existing ~/.zprofile ran brew shellenv after nix-darwin initialized PATH. Added a Home Manager-managed ~/.zprofile preserving Homebrew environment, OrbStack integration, and ~/.local/bin while restoring /etc/profiles/per-user/scaf/bin ahead of Homebrew. Revised flake check and full no-link Darwin build pass. A second activation is required before final command-resolution and shell checks.
Second activation and final verification passed: active system matches expected; Home Manager manages ~/.zprofile while preserving Homebrew and OrbStack setup; all 12 commands resolve via /etc/profiles/per-user/scaf/bin; 12/12 smoke tests pass; interactive zsh exits cleanly and exposes fzf-file-widget; generated Brewfile excludes all 12 requests and bundle check passes. Final two-axis review found no blockers or spec defects; acceptance MET.
close_reason: Migrated the 12 selected CLI tools to Home Manager, activated successfully, verified Nix path precedence and shell integration, passed smoke tests, and completed final review.

title: Validate reproducible Mac bootstrap and documentation
description: Verify the final repository can provision the intended Nix/Home Manager/Homebrew state from a clean or isolated test context. Update README commands, prerequisites, work-laptop limitations, secret restoration, and manual post-install steps.
acceptance_criteria: flake check and darwin build pass; documented bootstrap commands match the flake output; all intentionally managed software is represented; secrets are excluded; and remaining manual steps are explicit.
notes: Final bootstrap documentation added to README: prerequisites, existing/first nix-darwin activation commands, exact validation and generation checks, Homebrew cleanup warning and compatibility-shim lifecycle, package ownership, mutable npm/uv reinstall inventory, secret restoration/exclusion, manual macOS permissions, work-laptop restrictions, rollback, and X220 commands. A tracked-files-only isolated copy under /private/tmp passed flake check and full macbook-pro build; generated Brewfile has 32 brew lines, 15 casks, and 6 taps; macbook-pro/x220 selectors resolve; pinned first-install darwin-rebuild target builds; exact documented validation and Homebrew commands pass; current npm/uv exceptions match docs; tracked secret-pattern scan is clean. Parallel standards/spec review found no blockers and acceptance MET.
close_reason: Validated a tracked-only isolated bootstrap and documented prerequisites, exact commands, ownership, mutable exceptions, secrets, manual steps, work constraints, and rollback.

title: Enable Homebrew cleanup after migration parity
description: After all migration categories are resolved, review brew leaves, autoremove candidates, taps, services, and casks. Change nix-darwin Homebrew activation cleanup from none to the agreed mode only after a dry run and rollback review. Do not remove application data or credentials.
acceptance_criteria: All remaining Homebrew entries are intentional and declared, stale taps/dependencies are removed, brew doctor has no migration-caused failures, cleanup is safely enabled or explicitly deferred, and a rollback generation is known.
notes:
Pre-activation cleanup manifest (dry-run SHA-256 d6befae0ab9d48ec5f9ca9b96a8986ccd67da8bd47d8ba896e34c565ea90d16e): formulae proposed for removal: shellcheck, actionlint, age, pycparser, cffi, cryptography, libyaml, tree, ansible, libnet, arping, awscli, azure-cli, ncurses, bash, biome, libgit2, eza, fd, sdl2-compat, fzf, gdk-pixbuf, gh, jbig2dec, json-c, libidn, ghostscript, jasper, netpbm, gts, librsvg, graphviz, helm, libde265, libheif, imagemagick, k6, kubectx, lazygit, liblinear, lua, mkcert, nmap, nspr, nss, sops, sshpass, wireguard-go, wireguard-tools, xorriso, fluxcd/tap/flux. Taps proposed for removal: derailed/k9s, hashicorp/tap, wezterm/wezterm, fluxcd/tap, localstack/tap, kitlangton/tap. No casks are proposed for removal. Homebrew also proposes only caches, old keg versions, and temporary/vendor files under its normal cleanup phase.

Rollback: the immediate pre-cleanup configuration is /nix/var/nix/profiles/system-14-link -> /nix/store/jj3939z8wc0r7fq3ap5c6s988s6dkh5r-darwin-system-25.11.ebec37a and can be reactivated with its activate script. Homebrew removals are not restored by Nix generation rollback; the original 57-formula/15-cask baseline Brewfile is retained by generation 9 at /nix/store/1v8p14rxvs8vlbdqk7b2djval9rnfj6y-Brewfile and can reinstall the baseline with brew bundle install --no-upgrade. The baseline also remains reconstructible from git commit 3bc86d1.
Activation attempt failed safely before package installation/removal: pinned nix-darwin 25.11 generated Homebrew's removed 'brew bundle --cleanup' option. A minimal non-mutating repro on Homebrew 7.0.2 confirmed the option-parser failure. Current nix-darwin master uses --force-cleanup but cannot be paired with pinned nixpkgs 25.11 due release checks, so the fix keeps cleanup=none in the old module and appends a compatibility activation step that runs the supported 'brew bundle cleanup --force' subcommand after the normal install. Generated activation script asserts the obsolete form absent and supported form present; flake/full build pass. Homebrew metadata auto-updated during diagnosis, but no formula/cask upgraded or installed. Updated dry-run still proposes the identical 51 formulae, six taps, and zero casks; only one extra Homebrew cache entry changed the dry-run hash to 026aaa0b543c2fe61990ab3cff9cc24d09785ad6e50e6d4cbdf1e9944b36e7c6.
Post-activation reconciliation: initial Homebrew 7 cleanup removed the declared migration set but could not inspect four installed formulae from untrusted taps (k9s 0.50.18, terraform 1.14.3, ghui 0.7.1, localstack-cli 4.14.0), so they and the six stale taps were removed explicitly. Cleanup then exposed the installed formula rename sdl2 -> sdl2-compat; it is required by retained ffmpeg/mpv, so a targeted brew upgrade migrated that dependency and necessarily upgraded its two dependents (ffmpeg 8.0.1->9.0.2, mpv 0.41.0->0.41.0_10). Both media workflows pass and ~/.config/mpv remains intact; no global Homebrew mpv config existed. sdl2-compat is now declared explicitly. A second cleanup removed 31 newly identifiable unused dependencies and old kegs/caches. Final bundle check passes, cleanup reports no removals (only a non-fatal stale libtiff/webp graph warning), brew missing is empty, exactly six declared taps remain, all 15 casks remain, and brew doctor has no missing-dependency/untrusted/stale-tap migration warnings. Remaining doctor warnings are only deprecated whisky/gemini-cli, CLT update, and Tier 2 status.
Final activation verification: /run/current-system matches expected generation qm926nx...; final Brewfile is satisfied; cleanup exits 0 with no removals (only upstream stale libtiff/webp metadata warning); brew missing empty; exactly six declared taps and all 15 casks remain; doctor has no migration-caused warnings; retained and migrated commands resolve correctly. Final standards/spec review found no blockers and acceptance MET. The compatibility shim must be removed together with cleanup=none when nix-darwin is upgraded beyond 25.11; this is documented adjacent to the code and will be called out in bootstrap documentation.
close_reason: Enabled safe non-zap Homebrew reconciliation with a Homebrew 7 compatibility shim, removed all stale formulae/taps/dependencies, preserved casks and data, validated media/runtime behavior, and reached an idempotent declared state.

title: Migrate media, networking, and native utility formulae
description: Evaluate the remaining standard formulae such as arping, ffmpeg, ghostscript, mpv, neovim, nmap, nss, sshpass, terminal-notifier, tree-sitter, tree-sitter-cli, wireguard-tools, and xorriso. Verify macOS integrations, codecs, plugins, and runtime behavior; leave a formula in Homebrew if the Nix build is materially less functional.
acceptance_criteria: Each candidate has a tested destination, selected Nix-managed tools work for actual use cases, retained Homebrew exceptions are documented, and Neovim migration does not overwrite the existing dirty ~/.config/nvim repository.
notes:
Implemented pre-activation candidate: migrated arping, ghostscript, nmap, nss, sshpass, wireguard-tools, and xorriso to Home Manager. Retained ffmpeg (newer codec build), mpv (native macOS integration), Neovim (newer binary and unmanaged dirty config), terminal-notifier (newer native binary), and tree-sitter pair (aligned with Neovim), with reasons documented in code. Flake check, full no-link build, Brewfile and bundle checks pass. Pre-activation two-axis review found no blockers; runtime checks remain.
First post-activation check found pkgs.nss installs only libraries, leaving certutil resolved from Homebrew. Corrected ownership to pkgs.nss.tools. Rebuilt successfully and verified all seven representative workflows directly from selected Nix outputs; one additional activation is required to expose NSS tools in the Home Manager profile.
Final activation verification passed: active generation matches; all seven migrated commands resolve from Home Manager; all representative workflows pass; retained exceptions resolve from Homebrew; interactive zsh is clean; ~/.config/nvim remains an unmanaged non-symlink Git repo with its dirty state preserved. Final standards/spec review found no blockers and acceptance MET.
close_reason: Migrated seven portable utilities to Home Manager, documented six native/version-sensitive Homebrew exceptions, activated twice to correct NSS output selection, and verified all runtime workflows.
